title: Relative H1-regular immersions in locally finitely presented ambient schemes are universally Koszul-regular
statement: Let $P\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $i:Z\to P$ be an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume $Z\to S$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Assume also that, locally at every point of $Z$, $i$ is a closed immersion into an open subscheme of $P$ whose ideal is generated by a finite $H_1$-regular sequence, meaning a sequence with vanishing first Koszul homology [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. For every morphism $S'\to S$, the base-changed immersion $Z\times_SS'\to P\times_SS'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is Koszul-regular: locally at every source point it is a closed immersion into an open subscheme whose ideal is generated by a finite sequence with all positive Koszul homology zero. This includes $S'=S$ and allows empty sequences. No flatness of $P\to S$ or of $S'\to S$, and no Noetherian hypothesis, is assumed.

source.place: Tag 063V (lemma-flat-relative-H1-regular), conclusion (2), retaining its Koszul-regular consequence; relative H1-regular means definition-relative-H1-regular-immersion. Regular immersions are Koszul-regular by the regular-immersion definitions and regular-sequence Koszul acyclicity.

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$ and its image $s\in S$. Work in a closed-immersion neighbourhood supplied by the hypothesis. Using [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], choose an affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and an affine ambient chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ around $i(z)$ with $B$ finitely presented over $A$, contained in that neighbourhood. Principal refinements preserve finite presentation: if $B=A[x]/(g)$, then $B_h=A[x,t]/(g,ht-1)$. Thus we can retain a finite sequence $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ cutting out $Z\cap\operatorname{Spec}B=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$, $I=(f)$, with $H_1(K_B(f))=0$. Here the hypothesis's finite generators restrict to sections on the chart, and the affine closed-immersion description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies its ideal. Generation and first-homology vanishing can be checked by localization: the localized Koszul complex is the germ complex by [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso], and exact localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] identifies its homology with localized homology. A nonzero class in either the ideal modulo the generated subideal or this homology would survive at a maximal ideal containing its annihilator: otherwise a scalar outside that maximal ideal would annihilate it. Thus vanishing at all germs proves both assertions on the affine chart. Outside the source one equation is a unit and the exterior-wedge contraction written in step 7 gives vanishing. Koszul restriction is scalar extension by [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso], and localization is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so principal refinements preserve the asserted first-homology vanishing. The source restriction is flat over $\operatorname{Spec}A$: its local-ring maps are those of $Z\to S$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] gives $A$-flatness of $B/I$. Let $Q\supseteq I$ correspond to $i(z)$.

source.place: Tag 063V (lemma-flat-relative-H1-regular), first paragraph; affine chart meaning of the stated hypothesis, with principal refinements written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-h1-flat-quotient-ambient-flat-neighbourhood] to $A\to B$, $f$, and $Q$. Obtain $h\notin Q$ such that $B_h$ is $A$-flat. Replace the chart by $D(h)$ and replace $B,I,f,Q$ by their restrictions. Finite presentation persists by the displayed presentation in step 1. The quotient is $(B/I)_h$, still $A$-flat by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness]. The localized Koszul complex is the Koszul complex of the localized sequence by [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso]; exactness of localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] preserves exactness in degree one. Consequently the new chart has all three properties needed below: $B/A$ flat and finitely presented, $B/I$ flat over $A$, and $H_1(K_B(f))=0$.

source.place: Tag 063V, use of conclusion (1) before the final application of lemma-relative-regular-immersion-flat-in-neighbourhood.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak p=Q\cap A$ and $F=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-h1-flat-quotient-base-change-surjective] with $A'=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Its source is zero, since $H_1(K_B(f))=0$, so $H_1(K_F(\bar f))=0$. The finite presentation of $B$ gives a finite presentation, in particular finite generation, of $F$ over the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by tensoring its displayed polynomial presentation. Thus $F$ is Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. The fibre prime $\bar Q$ corresponding to $Q$ can be described by localizing $B$ at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and reducing modulo $\mathfrak p$: the prime $Q$ survives the localization and contains $\mathfrak pB$, so gives a prime of $F$, with contraction $Q$. This is the fibre-ring description of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 063U (lemma-relative-regular-immersion-flat-in-neighbourhood), fibre step; more-algebra.tex Tag 063Q supplies the H1 base-change assertion.

proof.text: The ring $F_{\bar Q}$ is nonzero local, and it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Localizing the degree-one exactness from step 3, using [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], gives $H_1(K_{F_{\bar Q}}(\bar f/1))=0$. By [lem-per-h1-koszul-quasi-regular], the canonical polynomial-to-associated-graded map for this localized sequence is an isomorphism. All its elements lie in the maximal ideal, since $I\subseteq Q$. Therefore [lem-pur-quasi-regular-noetherian-local] applies and makes this sequence regular in $F_{\bar Q}$. This proves that the fibre-local ideal $IF_{\bar Q}$ is generated by a regular sequence; no Noetherian hypothesis on $A$ or $B$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 063U, conversion of the Noetherian fibre sequence to regularity; more-algebra.tex Tags 062I and 09CC, and algebra.tex lemma-quasi-regular-regular.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-flat-quotient-fiber-regular-sequence] with $(R,A,I,Q,P)$ there equal to $(A,B,I,Q,\bar Q)$ here (use tensor symmetry to interchange the order of the fibre factors). The ambient map is flat and finitely presented by step 2, $I$ is finitely generated, the quotient is $A$-flat, and step 4 verifies its fibre-local regular-ideal hypothesis. Obtain $g\notin Q$ such that $C=B_g$ has $IC=(a_1,\ldots,a_c)$ generated by a finite $C$-regular sequence. The ambient algebra $C$ is flat over $A$ by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness], and is finitely presented by the presentation of a principal localization in step 1. Its quotient $C/IC=(B/I)_g$ is $A$-flat by the same localization-flatness statement. We may therefore use these new regular generators instead of the original $H_1$-regular list on the neighbourhood $D(g)$ of $i(z)$.

source.place: Tag 063U, lifting the fibre regular ideal to a regular-immersion neighbourhood; affine lifting form of Tag 063W(2) (lemma-fibre-quasi-regular).

proof.text: Let $A\to A'$ be any ring map and set $C'=C\otimes_AA'$, $a_j'=a_j\otimes1$, $J'=(a_1',\ldots,a_c')$. For every prime $Q'\supseteq J'$, [lem-pur-relative-regular-equations-base-change] applies to the regular generators of step 5: $C/A$ is flat and finitely presented and $C/(a)$ is $A$-flat. It gives regularity of the ordered list $a'/1$ in $C'_{Q'}$. Hence all its positive Koszul homology vanishes by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular]. This use imposes no flatness on $A'$, and is made at every source point, not at arbitrary points where the quotient might be zero.

source.place: Tag 063U and Tag 0FUD (remark-relative-regular-immersion-elements), arbitrary base-change conclusion; more-algebra.tex Tag 062F.

proof.text: In fact $K_{C'}(a')$ is acyclic in positive degrees on the whole affine chart. At primes containing $J'$ this is step 6. At any other prime some $a_j'$ is invertible; on the localized exterior complex set $H(w)=(a_j')^{-1}e_j\wedge w$. The differential formula in [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] gives $dH+Hd=1$, so every cycle is a boundary. By [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso] and exactness of localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], these local homology modules are the localizations of $H_n(K_{C'}(a'))$. If a module has a nonzero element $v$, choose a maximal ideal containing its proper annihilator. Then $v/1$ is nonzero there, since $v/1=0$ would give an annihilating scalar outside that maximal ideal. Thus a module whose prime localizations all vanish is zero. Applied to each $n>0$, this proves the required Koszul-regularity of $a'$ in $C'$.

source.place: Tag 063V(2), regular-to-Koszul consequence; explicit localization and unit-contraction argument after more-algebra.tex Tag 062F.

proof.text: Finally let $S'\to S$ be arbitrary and $z'\in Z\times_SS'$ with image $z\in Z$. Choose the chart $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of step 5 around $z$, and an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A'\subset S'$ around the parameter image of $z'$ mapping into $\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], the product chart is open in $P\times_SS'$ and contains the image of $z'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] it is $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_AA')$. Its closed source has coordinate ring $(C/(a))\otimes_AA'\cong C'/J'$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] to $C\to C'$ and $(a)$, and identify $C'\otimes_C(C/(a))$ with $A'\otimes_A(C/(a))$ by $(c\otimes t)\otimes\bar b\mapsto t\otimes\overline{cb}$, with inverse $t\otimes\bar b\mapsto(1\otimes t)\otimes\bar b$. These mutually inverse maps respect the projections. Step 7 supplies finite Koszul-regular equations for this source. Since every $z'$ has such a neighbourhood, this is the assertion. For the identity base change take $A'=A$. If a source or base-change chart is empty there is no point to check; if the sequence is empty, its Koszul complex is concentrated in degree zero and every preceding argument still applies.

source.place: Tag 063V(2), local-to-global conclusion, using affine fibre products and the quotient tensor formula.
